findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, meaning data is stored unencrypted by default rather than using SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS.

findings.issue_category: no bucket ACL / public access controls
findings.description: No acl attribute is set and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource, leaving the bucket to potentially inherit default/public access settings and no explicit protection against public exposure.
The bucket stores ledger export data (likely sensitive financial data) without any server_side_encryption_configuration, exposing data at rest if storage is compromised.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket to explicitly block public ACLs/policies, relying only on the default 'private' ACL which can be overridden.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket containing operational runbooks, leaving data unencrypted at rest.

findings.issue_category: invalid/malformed ACL likely granting unintended access
findings.description: The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid canned ACL (the valid value would be 'log-delivery-write'); this typo could cause deployment failure or unexpected default/broader access behavior for an audit log bucket, undermining the integrity of the audit trail.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption / plaintext sensitive file upload
findings.description: The vendor roster file is uploaded to a bucket without server-side encryption enabled and without specifying any object-level encryption (kms_key_id or server_side_encryption), potentially exposing sensitive vendor data at rest.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be destroyed without recovery, which combined with lack of versioning increases risk of irreversible data loss that could be leveraged in an attack or accidental deletion.
